subject: Inference health snapshot & QBR action requests
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inference health snapshot & QBR action requests

Team —

Attached is the monthly snapshot (2026-10-kpi-dashboard.pdf) I pulled for the QBR prep. High-level notes first-pass:

- Latency: p50 = 62ms (+4ms MoM), p95 = 340ms (spike on 10/01 correlated with model rollout).
- Cost: hosting cost per 1M tokens = $220 (up 7% MoM); embeddings cost steady.
- Uptime: 99.96% (two brief incidents on 10/01 and 10/03 impacting a subset of EU endpoints).
- Usage: active requests up 18% MoM; chat-prod concurrency increase is the primary driver.

As part of QBR we need:
1) A short slide summarizing the p95 spike root cause and mitigation (owner: Markus).
2) Cost optimization opportunities and downside risk if we throttle (owner: Rishi).
3) Operational note on the EU incidents and customer impact (owner: Laura).
4) Ask for a 1-page explainer on KV cache hit improvements and expected cost delta (owner: Stephanie).

Please review the dashboard and reply with any clarifying items or objections to the owners above. If you can’t own an item, propose the alternate owner and a due date.

Attachments: 2026-10-kpi-dashboard.pdf (PDF)

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Platform Ops, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700

Thanks Lauren — quick read-through below and I've CC'd Marcus and Stephanie for infra/serving context.

On Sun, Oct 4, 2026 at 08:12 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Attached is the monthly snapshot (2026-10-kpi-dashboard.pdf) I pulled for the QBR prep. High-level notes first-pass:
> 
> - Latency: p50 = 62ms (+4ms MoM), p95 = 340ms (spike on 10/01 correlated with model rollout).
> 
The p95 spike lines up with the 10/01 rollout of the v2-small quantized variant we deployed in eu-west-1 to relieve capacity pressure. Early telemetry shows an unexpected cold-start pattern on multi-model hosts (some kernels falling back to CPU for a few minutes).

I'll take owner for the root-cause slide. Action plan I'm proposing:
- Collect kernel-level traces from the 10/01 window (Marcus to pull).
- Add a note on the slide about temporary fallback to CPU and ETA for a fix (2-3 days to backfill hot kernels).

I'll coordinate with Marcus and Stephanie to get traces and a concise blurb for the deck.

—Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Serving Runtime
markus.klein@redwood.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference health snapshot & QBR action requests

+1 to Markus' assessment. I pulled a quick comparison of batch-size distribution and KV cache hit rates for chat-prod (attached summary will go into the QBR notes). Highlights:

- KV cache hit improved from 47% -> 62% after the 9/20 tuning, which reduced CPU cycles per request but increased GPU memory pressure for larger batches.
- The 10/01 rollout introduced a host mix with slightly older CUDA drivers that degraded kernel selection; that produced the short p95 blips Markus mentioned.

Proposed operational changes:
- Temporarily cap max batch size on eu-west-1 chat-prod from 128 -> 96 for the next 72 hours while we push the updated kernels. Owner: Rishi (can you confirm asap?)
- Add a single-slide explanation of cache hit improvements and the work item to reduce memory pressure (owner: Stephanie, due 10/09).

Attachments: cost-analysis-optimization-notes.xlsx (XLSX)

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Platform Reliability
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

Acknowledged — I can own the short-term cap on batch size and the cost delta estimate. Quick notes:

- I'll schedule the batch-size cap change for 10/07 11:00 PDT (72-hour window). If we see regression in throughput we'll revert and notify affected customers.
- I'll produce a cost sensitivity table showing cost vs throughput tradeoffs (deliverable by 10/09 EOD).
- Laura, if the EU incidents affected Acme Cloud, can you coordinate customer comms? If so, please flag any notes we should include in the QBR's "customer impact" slide.

- Stephanie: 1-slide on KV cache improvements and memory-pressure mitigation (deliverable 10/09) — noted in cost notes.
